misreading: The equal-cost tie-break vector maps an absent package to Version 0.0.0 (unwrap_or), so absence ties with 0.0.0 instead of sorting below it (R32). Separately, provenance paths are built in one alphabetical pass over selected packages with each dependency processed once, so a package visited before its own parent extends an empty/stale source path: evidence and MissingFeature.path lack the root token or are not the shortest (R45-R47).
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: No visible test has equal-cost solutions differing by absent-vs-0.0.0, and no visible error reports evidence/paths for chains where a child name sorts before its parent.
prevention: Never encode 'absent' with a sentinel equal to a legal value; and recompute derived data (paths, distances) to a true fixpoint, independent of iteration order.

misreading: MissingFeature is checked after Conflict and NoMatch, but R43 inserts it between Missing and Conflict, so nodes with both a missing feature and a conflict/no-match report the wrong error (and the wrong first failing leaf). Also, dependency origins are recorded from not-yet-final source paths: a stale shorter path survives in paths and a second origin with the correct path is appended, giving two evidence entries for one edge (R47).
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: The only visible feature test succeeds; no visible test has a node where MissingFeature competes with Conflict/NoMatch or inspects evidence for multi-level chains.
prevention: When a spec inserts a check into an existing precedence chain, place it exactly where stated and test every adjacent pair of competing errors.

misreading: The position-two '=' pending state is mis-tracked. F1/F2 never reset the group length after 'xx==' (F2 also never emits the byte), so every input ending in '==' (e.g. Zh==) returns Truncated. F3 stores '=' as raw byte 61 in the digit array, colliding with digit '9' (value 61): Zm9= decodes to 'f', an unpadded group with '9' third hits unreachable! panic, and its R7 guard (len==2) is dead so a non-'=' after pending '=' gives InvalidByte or panics instead of BadPadding.
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: Visible decode tests only exercise a single '=' (T2s=) and unpadded groups without digit 61 in position two; no xx== or pending-padding error input.
prevention: Turn every example in the spec into a test, trace each state-machine path to EOF, and never store sentinels in the same domain as data.

misreading: decode_many preallocates Vec::with_capacity(count) from the caller's count; for huge counts (e.g. usize::MAX) this panics with 'capacity overflow' from layout arithmetic before any byte is read, instead of returning the first integer's Truncated error. R18's 'must not panic on any count' (allocation exhaustion excluded) targets exactly this; the decoders are otherwise correct.
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: Visible batch tests use count 0 and 2; none passes an enormous count against a short input.
prevention: Never preallocate from an untrusted count or length; bound capacity by what the input can supply and test with usize::MAX arguments.

misreading: Signed-zero numeric edge cases: F1, F2 and F4 accept '-0' as Integer 0 (the zero branch ignores the minus sign) although R33 forbids -0; F3 handles -0 but rejects every negative decimal with zero integral part, including '-0.01' which R34 says is valid. Non-shared extras: F1 stops evaluating a row after its first error under Collect (R37); F2 pushes each UTF-8 byte as a char when quoting, corrupting non-ASCII quoted fields (R51/R54).
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: The only visible typed test uses positive values (12, 4.50); no negative-zero spellings, no Collect errors, and no non-ASCII quoted writer output.
prevention: For numeric grammars, explicitly test signed-zero forms (-0, -0.00, -0.01) and every spelling the spec names as valid or invalid.

misreading: next_fire brute-forces minute by minute and recomputes the weekday by looping over every year since 2000 on each step, so an unrealizable schedule that must return None (e.g. '0 0 30 2 *') or a rare one (Feb 29 on a given weekday) scans ~210M minutes x O(years), timing out. F2 additionally panics on bases like '**'/'*5' (b'*'-b'0' underflow, R8) and validates the step before base numbers (R11 order).
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: Visible next_fire tests find a match within at most ~14 months, so the worst-case full-range scan is never exercised.
prevention: Estimate worst-case iterations, especially no-result searches, and skip whole non-matching units (days, months) instead of brute-forcing the finest granularity.
